Re: Appeal of denial for total shoulder replacement  
Member: Taylor Jennings  
Member ID: W164265496  
Reference number: POC-209DEB4204-66822  
Requested procedure: CPT 23472, total shoulder replacement

Dear Appeals Department:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for my total shoulder replacement. Please conduct a complete reconsideration of the request based on the clinical records already submitted and the additional explanation in this appeal.

The record documents an extensive and unsuccessful course of conservative treatment:

- I have had progressive shoulder pain for 14 months despite rest.
- I completed 24 supervised physical-therapy visits over 16 weeks, from March 8, 2026, through June 28, 2026. Therapy focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening, and the physical-therapy discharge note documents completion.
- I used NSAIDs for six months without adequate relief.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on May 12, 2026. It provided only four weeks of partial relief.
- Despite these measures, I continue to have substantial pain and functional impairment.

The records also establish advanced structural disease and significant loss of function. Shoulder radiographs dated July 14, 2026, show complete loss of the glenohumeral joint space, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid. CT imaging confirms an intact rotator cuff. On examination, I have glenohumeral crepitus, active forward elevation limited to 90 degrees, and external rotation limited to 10 degrees, with intact cuff strength. I cannot reach overhead, dress without help, or sleep on the affected side.

The record further documents that there is no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a nonsmoker. These findings support proceeding with the requested surgery and do not identify a documented contraindication. The procedure was requested by Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery.

This appeal directly addresses the stated concern about insufficient conservative treatment. The clinical record shows prolonged symptoms, medication treatment, an injection trial, and a completed supervised physical-therapy program, all with inadequate or temporary benefit. Continuing the same conservative measures would not reasonably address the documented end-stage glenohumeral joint disease and severe functional limitations.

No publicly available governing Commercial/ACA medical policy for CPT 23472 was identified or quoted in preparing this appeal. Please provide the specific medical-necessity criteria, policy or guideline name, policy number, version or effective date, and clinical-review rationale applied to this request. If the plan relies on a requirement for a particular duration, type, or sequence of conservative treatment, please identify that requirement and explain how the submitted records fail to satisfy it.

Based on the documented failed conservative treatment, advanced imaging findings, severe functional impairment, and orthopedic evaluation, I respectfully request that the denial be reversed and authorization be issued for CPT 23472.

Please send the appeal determination and any additional information requests in writing. If the appeal cannot be approved, please provide the specific clinical basis for the decision and the applicable external-review rights.

Sincerely,

Taylor Jennings
